```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4.2)
library(nlmixr2lib)
library(PKNCA)
library(rxode2)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
```

# Model and source

Lei 2018 is a veterinary pharmacokinetic/pharmacodynamic integration study of
**florfenicol** against *Streptococcus suis* in pigs. Eight healthy pigs
received 30 mg/kg intramuscularly and, after a two-week washout,
intravenously. Plasma drawn after the intramuscular dose was then used *ex
vivo* to build 24 h time-kill curves against *S. suis* serotype 2 strain
WH-2, and the 24 h change in bacterial count was related to the PK/PD index
AUC0-24h/MIC with an inhibitory sigmoid Emax model fitted in WinNonlin.

The pharmacokinetics were analysed non-compartmentally only, so the paper's
one quantitative model is the sigmoid PK/PD-integration curve, and that is
what the package carries. Exposure enters as the covariate `AUC_FLOR`.

* Article: <https://doi.org/10.3389/fphar.2018.00002>

```{r model}
mod_fun <- readModelDb("Lei_2018_florfenicol_pkpd_index")
mod <- rxode2::rxode(mod_fun)
cat(mod$reference, "\n")
```

```{r description, results = "asis"}
cat(mod$description, "\n")
```

# Population

Eight healthy pigs (four male, four female) weighing 15-20 kg were housed
individually with antibiotic-free feed and water at Huazhong Agricultural
University, Wuhan, China. The Animals section gives their age as 8-10 weeks
and the PK design section as 4-5 weeks. Each received a single 30 mg/kg
intramuscular dose of a 30% florfenicol injection and, after a 2-week washout,
the same dose intravenously; plasma was sampled from 0.25 h to 196 h and
assayed by HPLC (LLOQ 0.05 ug/mL). The free fraction in pooled plasma was
85 +/- 3.3%.

The challenge organism, *S. suis* serotype 2 strain WH-2, was chosen from 124
clinical isolates collected across China in 2015-2017 (MIC50 = 1 ug/mL,
MIC90 = 2 ug/mL, Figure 1) because its MIC equals the MIC90. Its florfenicol
MIC is 2 ug/mL and MBC 4 ug/mL in both broth and pig plasma, and its mutant
prevention concentration is 3.2 ug/mL. For the *ex vivo* curves about 10^6
CFU/mL of WH-2 was incubated for 24 h in plasma drawn at 0-24 h after the
intramuscular dose.

```{r population}
str(mod$population)
```

# Source trace

| Quantity | Value | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Model form | `E = e0 - (e0 - emax) * C^N / (C^N + EC50^N)`, `C = AUC0-24h/MIC` | Methods Equation 1 (garbled as printed; see Errata), Figure 6 |
| `e0` | 2.36 log10 CFU/mL | Table 3, row 'Emax' (footnote: change in the blank sample) |
| `emax` | -6.00 log10 CFU/mL | Not printed; lower asymptote of Figure 6 'Predicted' curve, digitised by the maintainers |
| `lec50` | log(42.22 h) | Table 3, EC50 = 42.22 +/- 1.20 h |
| `lhill` | log(9.89) | Table 3, N = 9.89 +/- 1.15 |
| `mic` | 2 ug/mL (fixed) | Results, 'MIC, MBC, and MPC of WH-2' |
| `log10_cfu0` | 6 (fixed) | Methods, ex vivo time-killing curves (10^6 CFU/ml) |
| `addSd` | 0 (fixed) | Not reported (only R^2 = 0.999, Discussion) |
| `AUC_FLOR` (covariate) | 88.85 h*ug/mL after 30 mg/kg IM | Table 1 (AUC0-24h, IM); Table 2 index 44.43 h = 88.85 / 2 |
| `d/dt(bact)` | `ln(10) * (E / 24) * bact` | Library convention spreading the 24 h change uniformly; E is defined over 24 h (Methods) |

# Back-solving the published targets

Table 3 reports the AUC0-24h/MIC needed for three effect levels. Inverting the
sigmoid with the packaged parameters gives the index at which each level is
reached; this is the check that `e0`, `emax`, EC50 and N were transcribed and
assembled correctly, and it uses no value that was itself derived from these
targets.

```{r targets}
theta <- setNames(mod$iniDf$est, mod$iniDf$name)
p <- list(
  e0 = theta[["e0"]], emax = theta[["emax"]],
  ec50 = exp(theta[["lec50"]]), hill = exp(theta[["lhill"]]), mic = theta[["mic"]]
)
sigmoid_inverse <- function(E, e0, emax, ec50, hill) {
  f <- (e0 - E) / (e0 - emax)
  ec50 * (f / (1 - f))^(1 / hill)
}
targets <- tibble::tibble(
  activity = c("Bacteriostatic", "Bactericidal", "Eradication"),
  E = c(0, -3, -4),
  published = c(37.89, 44.02, 46.42)
) |>
  mutate(
    model = sigmoid_inverse(E, p$e0, p$emax, p$ec50, p$hill),
    pct_diff = 100 * (model / published - 1)
  )
targets |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Activity" = activity, "E (log10 CFU/mL)" = E,
    "Published AUC0-24h/MIC (h)" = published, "Model AUC0-24h/MIC (h)" = model,
    "Difference (%)" = pct_diff
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2)

# All three published targets are reproduced to within 2.5%; a mis-transcribed
# EC50 or Hill coefficient, or the literal (garbled) Equation 1, moves them by
# far more (the literal equation cannot reach E = -3 at all).
stopifnot(all(abs(targets$pct_diff) < 2.5))
```

The model places every target 1.4-2.2% above the published value. The same
small, same-signed offset appears whichever way the unprinted maximal effect is
resolved (see Assumptions and deviations), so it is a property of how Lei 2018
computed the targets rather than of the encoding.

# The packaged ODE reproduces the 24 h change

The model integrates the bacterial density so that `log10(bact)` changes by
exactly the sigmoid effect over a 24 h incubation. One "subject" per index
level checks the solved ODE against the closed form.

```{r ode-check}
idx_grid <- c(0, 10, 20, 30, 35, 38, 40, 42.22, 44, 46, 48, 50, 55, 60)
ev <- tibble::tibble(id = seq_along(idx_grid), AUC_FLOR = idx_grid * p$mic)
ev <- bind_rows(
  mutate(ev, time = 0),
  mutate(ev, time = 24)
) |>
  mutate(evid = 0, amt = 0, cmt = "bact") |>
  arrange(id, time)
sim <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod, events = ev, keep = "AUC_FLOR") |>
  as.data.frame() |>
  filter(time == 24) |>
  mutate(
    aucmic = AUC_FLOR / p$mic,
    change_ode = log10(bact) - theta[["log10_cfu0"]],
    change_closed = p$e0 - (p$e0 - p$emax) * aucmic^p$hill / (aucmic^p$hill + p$ec50^p$hill)
  )
# Both sides use the same parameters, so the difference is pure ODE solver
# error and a tight bound is correct.
stopifnot(max(abs(sim$change_ode - sim$change_closed)) < 1e-4)
sim |>
  select(aucmic, change_ode, change_closed) |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "AUC0-24h/MIC (h)" = aucmic, "24 h change, ODE" = change_ode,
    "24 h change, closed form" = change_closed
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 3)
```

# Replicating Figure 6

Figure 6 plots the observed 24 h change for each *ex vivo* plasma sample
against its AUC0-24h/MIC, with the fitted curve. The observed points below were
digitised by the maintainers from the published figure (about +/- 0.2 log10
CFU/mL); the hollow markers and overlapping points near the lower plateau limit
the precision.

```{r figure6}
# Digitised from Lei 2018 Figure 6 ('Observed').
fig6_obs <- tibble::tibble(
  aucmic = c(0, 16.0, 27.2, 36.5, 40.9, 45.4, 49.0, 49.7, 52.7, 53.2),
  effect = c(2.78, 2.40, 1.95, 1.00, 0.28, -4.65, -4.80, -4.80, -4.80, -4.80)
)
curve <- tibble::tibble(aucmic = seq(0, 60, by = 0.25)) |>
  mutate(effect = p$e0 - (p$e0 - p$emax) * aucmic^p$hill / (aucmic^p$hill + p$ec50^p$hill))

# Replicates Figure 6 of Lei 2018: ex vivo AUC0-24h/MIC versus the 24 h
# change in S. suis count in pig plasma.
ggplot(curve, aes(aucmic, effect)) +
  geom_line(colour = "blue") +
  geom_point(data = fig6_obs, shape = 1, colour = "red", size = 2.5) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = c(0, -3, -4), linetype = "dotted", colour = "grey50") +
  labs(
    x = "AUC0-24h/MIC (h)", y = "Change in log10 CFU/mL over 24 h",
    caption = "Replicates Figure 6 of Lei 2018. Line: packaged model; points: digitised observations."
  ) +
  theme_bw()
```

The packaged curve sits close to the published one. Its zero-exposure plateau
is the Table 3 value of 2.36, slightly below the published curve's plateau of
about 2.55 (see Assumptions and deviations).

# Probability of target attainment (Table 5)

Lei 2018 Table 5 gives the probability that AUC0-24h/MIC reaches the
bactericidal target after 30 mg/kg intramuscularly, at fixed MICs from 0.25 to
4 ug/mL, from a Crystal Ball Monte Carlo simulation that treated AUC0-24h as
log-normal with the Table 1 mean and SD (88.85 +/- 6.72 h*ug/mL). With a
log-normal AUC the attainment has a closed form, so no random draws are
needed.

```{r pta}
auc_mean <- 88.85
auc_sd <- 6.72
sdlog <- sqrt(log(1 + (auc_sd / auc_mean)^2))
meanlog <- log(auc_mean) - sdlog^2 / 2
pta <- function(target, mic) {
  100 * stats::plnorm(target * mic, meanlog, sdlog, lower.tail = FALSE)
}
mics <- c(0.25, 0.5, 1, 2, 4)
target_model <- targets$model[targets$activity == "Bactericidal"]
pta_tab <- tibble::tibble(
  mic = mics,
  published = c(100, 100, 100, 53.25, 0),
  pta_published_target = pta(44.02, mics),
  pta_model_target = pta(target_model, mics)
)
pta_tab |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "MIC (ug/mL)" = mic, "Published PTA (%)" = published,
    "PTA, published target 44.02 h (%)" = pta_published_target,
    "PTA, model target (%)" = pta_model_target
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = c(2, 2, 1, 1))

# Structural cells: certain attainment at MIC <= 1 and none at MIC = 4, for
# both targets. These hold regardless of where the target sits within a few
# percent, so they are the robust part of the table.
stopifnot(
  all(pta_tab$pta_model_target[pta_tab$mic <= 1] > 99.9),
  pta_tab$pta_model_target[pta_tab$mic == 4] < 0.1,
  # The published target reproduces the MIC = 2 cell to about 1 point.
  abs(pta_tab$pta_published_target[pta_tab$mic == 2] - 53.25) < 2
)
```

The structural cells (100% at MIC <= 1 ug/mL, 0% at 4 ug/mL) reproduce
exactly, and with the published target of 44.02 h the knife-edge MIC = 2 cell
reproduces the published 53.25% to within about one point. That cell sits on
the steep part of the attainment curve: the model's own bactericidal target is
1.7% higher, which moves it to about 45%. The PK/PD cut-off of 1 ug/mL (the
highest MIC with attainment of at least 90%) is the same either way.

# Dose prediction (Table 4)

Lei 2018 computes doses with
`Dose = (AUC/MIC) * MIC90 * CL / (fu * F)`, using MIC90 = 2 ug/mL,
fu = 0.85 and F = 0.9914. Table 4's 50% target-attainment column is the median
of a Monte Carlo distribution, which for this equation is close to the point
estimate. Using the intramuscular body clearance of 0.185 L/h/kg (Table 1):

```{r doses}
cl <- 0.185
fu <- 0.85
f_im <- 0.9914
dose_tab <- targets |>
  mutate(
    published_dose50 = c(16.50, 19.17, 20.14),
    dose_published_target = published * 2 * cl / (fu * f_im),
    dose_model_target = model * 2 * cl / (fu * f_im),
    pct_diff = 100 * (dose_model_target / published_dose50 - 1)
  )
dose_tab |>
  select(activity, published_dose50, dose_published_target, dose_model_target, pct_diff) |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Activity" = activity, "Published dose, 50% TAR (mg/kg)" = published_dose50,
    "Equation with published target (mg/kg)" = dose_published_target,
    "Equation with model target (mg/kg)" = dose_model_target,
    "Model vs published (%)" = pct_diff
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2)
stopifnot(all(abs(dose_tab$pct_diff) < 5))
```

The model-derived targets give doses 2-4% above the published 50%
column. The published 90% column (21.55, 25.02 and 26.85 mg/kg) depends on
the Monte Carlo spread of AUC, CL and fu, which Lei 2018 does not fully
specify, and is not reproduced here.

# Non-compartmental analysis

Lei 2018 published only non-compartmental pharmacokinetics (Table 1), and this
model contains no PK component, so there is no simulated concentration profile
to analyse with PKNCA. The relevant Table 1 quantity, the intramuscular
AUC0-24h of 88.85 h*ug/mL, enters the model directly as `AUC_FLOR`; Table 2's
AUC0-24h/MIC of 44.43 h equals 88.85 / 2, which confirms that the index uses
total plasma AUC and the 2 ug/mL MIC.

```{r index-check}
stopifnot(abs(88.85 / p$mic - 44.43) < 0.01)
```

# Assumptions and deviations

* **No compartmental PK model.** Lei 2018 analysed plasma concentrations
  non-compartmentally in WinNonlin 5.2.1. A one-compartment model cannot be
  derived from Table 1 consistently: the intravenous terminal rate
  (0.106 1/h) and clearance give V = 1.76 L/kg, but the intramuscular profile
  is flip-flop (terminal half-life 14.46 h against 6.54 h intravenously). If
  absorption is set to the intramuscular terminal rate, the predicted Tmax is
  13.7 h, not the published 4 h, and AUC0-24h is 77.5, not 88.85 h*ug/mL. If
  instead ka is set from the published Tmax, the intramuscular half-life becomes
  6.54 h and AUC0-24h about 143 h*ug/mL. Figure 5B shows a fast rise to a broad
  plateau followed by a slow decline, consistent with the sustained-release
  behaviour the authors describe, which needs more than first-order
  absorption. No PK file is therefore shipped; supply `AUC_FLOR` from Table 1
  or from another florfenicol PK model.
* **Maximal effect `emax` is not printed.** Table 3 lists 'Emax' (the
  zero-exposure value), EC50 and N but no drug-saturated effect, although the
  Results text says E0 was reported. It was digitised from the lower asymptote
  of the fitted curve in Figure 6 (-6.00 log10 CFU/mL). A free four-parameter
  sigmoid fitted to the digitised curve returns EC50 = 42.23 h and
  N = 9.97 against Table 3's 42.22 h and 9.89, so the drawn curve is the
  Table 3 fit.
* **Zero-exposure plateau: Table 3 versus Figure 6.** The same digitisation
  puts the drawn curve's plateau at about 2.55 log10 CFU/mL, against the
  Table 3 value of 2.36. Table 3's footnote defines its value as the change in
  the blank sample, and the blank curve in Figure 3B rises from about 6.4 to
  8.75 log10 CFU/mL (+2.35), so 2.36 may be the observed blank change rather
  than the fitted plateau. The printed table value is used. Using the
  figure's 2.55 instead moves the three targets to 2.1-2.6% above the
  published values, against 1.4-2.2% for the packaged choice.
* **Alternative back-solve.** Fitting both `e0` and `emax` to the three
  published targets alone (with Table 3's EC50 and N) gives e0 = 2.21 and
  emax = -6.43 and reproduces all three to 0.03%. That pair matches neither
  Table 3 nor Figure 6, so it was not adopted. The targets are reported as
  mean +/- SD, which suggests they were computed from per-sample or simulated
  values rather than from the mean curve.
* **Starting inoculum.** Methods state 10^6 CFU/mL; Figure 3 starts near
  6.4 log10 CFU/mL. The model predicts the change over 24 h, so only the
  starting point of a simulated trajectory depends on this choice.
* **Within-24 h shape.** The ODE spreads the 24 h change uniformly in log10
  space. Lei 2018 fitted only the 24 h endpoint; the shapes of the
  time-kill curves in Figure 3 are not part of the model.
* **Variability.** No between-animal variability or residual error was
  reported; the +/- values in Table 3 are uncertainties of the estimates.
  The model has no etas and `addSd` is fixed at 0.

# Errata

* **Equation 1 is garbled.** As printed it reads
  `E=Emax=(1-C^N/(C^N+EC50^N))`. Read as `E = Emax * (1 - f)` with
  Emax = 2.36 it ranges from 0 to 2.36 and cannot reach the paper's own E = -3
  or E = -4 targets. The standard inhibitory sigmoid form, whose fitted curve
  is drawn in Figure 6, is used instead.
* **Effect labels in the abstract and Methods.** The abstract assigns 37.89,
  44.02 and 46.42 h to bactericidal, bacteriostatic and elimination activity,
  and its doses 16.5, 19.17 and 20.14 mg/kg likewise. Tables 3 and 4 and the
  Results assign them to bacteriostatic (E = 0), bactericidal (E = -3) and
  eradication (E = -4); the tables are followed. Methods also describe
  E = -1 as a 99.9% and E = -3 as a 99.99% reduction, which do not match the
  Results' E = -3 and E = -4 definitions.
* **Table 5 effect label.** Table 5 labels its row 'Eradication', but the text
  states the bactericidal target of 44.02 h was used, and only that target
  reproduces the published 53.25% at MIC = 2 ug/mL; the eradication target of
  46.42 h gives about 27%. The text gives the same cell as 52.25%.
* **PK/PD cut-off.** The Results and Conclusion give the cut-off as
  1 ug/mL; the Discussion gives 0.5 ug/mL. Table 5 supports 1 ug/mL.
* **Unbound versus total exposure.** The Discussion says free plasma
  concentrations were integrated with the MIC, but Table 2's AUC0-24h/MIC of
  44.43 h equals the total AUC0-24h of 88.85 h*ug/mL divided by the
  2 ug/mL MIC. The model follows Table 2 and uses total exposure; the free
  fraction enters only the dose equation.
